summary: I sent the exact task prompt. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read the repo, and showed three candidate layouts as plain-text sample output in the terminal. It then asked me to pick one with AskUserQuestion. It never started a server, gave me a localhost URL, or wrote HTML. I picked option B (HEALTH column plus a "Failing checks" section). The agent then laid out the design in chat and asked for approval before writing any code. Once I said "yes, go ahead", it started TDD work on test/status.test.js and src/status.js. It wrote no spec file and no plan.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion was met, and the evidence for each comes from the session log tool_use list, greps of the log, and the state of the files on disk. The visual companion stayed closed, and the design happened in the terminal with text samples. The one oddity (the README bash command that looked hung) came after the design phase and doesn't affect the criteria.

observations.description: The README edit command began with `cat >> /dev/null; python3 - <<'EOF' ...`. The leading `cat` reads stdin, so the command looks like it hung: it had been running for 51s+ with a spinner when I stopped it with Ctrl+C. The README update may not have finished.
The agent made file edits with Bash+python string replacement (python3 heredoc doing s.replace) instead of the Edit tool. That is fragile and makes the diffs harder to review.

In the approval message the agent offered an unrequested extra (an unhealthy count in the heading) and asked me to say if I'd rather skip it. That's reasonable, but it's scope beyond what the user picked.
Startup needed three dialogs (theme, security notes, trust folder). On the trust and bypass dialogs, 'No, exit' is preselected.

criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in the session log was {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. It came before any Bash, Write or edit call.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion stayed closed (no start-server.sh, no localhost URL, no HTML screens)
criteria.evidence: The candidate layouts were plain text on screen (e.g. 'A: HEALTH column only.' with a sample table, then B and C), followed by an AskUserQuestion 'How should `svc status` show failing health checks?'. The tool_use list from the log is: Skill, Bash (git ls-files/cat), AskUserQuestion, Bash (python edit of test), Bash (npm test), Write src/status.js, Bash (README edit). None of them is start-server. Before my pick, grep -c for 'start-server|localhost|.html' in the log returned 0. A later grep matched only the skill's own description text, not tool calls. find for *.html in the workdir returned nothing.

The design stayed in chat: a short layout question, then a one-screen design ('Approach (all in src/status.js)… Testing (TDD…)') and 'Does this look right? Say yes and I'll implement it.' It did not go through the full spec-writing flow.
`ls docs` in the workdir gave 'No such file or directory'. git status --short showed only 'M src/status.js' and 'M test/status.test.js'. The only file_path in a Write/Edit call was src/status.js.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The only Skill tool_use in the log is hyperpowers:brainstorming. grep matches for 'writing-plans' all come from the skill listing or skill body text, not from an invocation. No plan file is on disk.

criteria.criterion: Asked for design approval before implementation code
criteria.evidence: After my pick the screen showed 'Here's the design for option B. I won't start until you approve it.' … 'Does this look right? Say yes and I'll implement it.' The log has no edit tool calls before my 'yes, go ahead'.
After approval the log shows a Bash python edit of test/status.test.js, then npm test, then Write src/status.js, then a README edit. git status shows src/status.js and test/status.test.js modified.
